paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We compare error rate (one minus accuracy), computation cost, and memory usage across our approach and baselines when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. MTL-FT refers to first fine-tuning a shared LoRA on all the datasets, and then fine-tuning the low-rank adapter on each dataset, while Full FT refers to full fine-tuning of the entire model. Our approach boosts the test accuracy of QLoRA by 10\% on average, only incurring 8\% additional computation and 9 GB more memory. It performs on par with the best baseline with 45\% less FLOPs.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart titled “QLoRA” illustrates a comparison of GPU memory usage (in GB) across six different fine-tuning methods for the Llama-3-8B model on ten NLP tasks, as described in the accompanying paper. The vertical y-axis represents GPU memory in gigabytes, ranging from 0 to above 60 GB with labeled tick marks at 0, 20, 40, and 60, using a linear scale. The horizontal x-axis lists the six methods: “Full FT,” “MTL-FT,” “TAG,” “LoRA,” “QLoRA,” and “Ours,” arranged in no particular order (not sorted by memory usage). Five of the bars are orange, while the bar for “Ours” is green, visually distinguishing the proposed method. “Full FT” exhibits the highest memory consumption, exceeding 60 GB. “MTL-FT” follows with approximately 40 GB. “TAG” and “LoRA” each consume around 20–25 GB. “QLoRA” uses the least memory among the orange bars, at roughly 15 GB. The “Ours” method, shown in green, uses approximately 25 GB — notably higher than QLoRA but significantly lower than Full FT and MTL-FT. The chart visually supports the claim in the caption that the proposed method incurs only 9 GB more memory than QLoRA, while achieving improved accuracy and reduced computation cost relative to other baselines.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart titled “QLoRA” illustrates the GPU memory usage (in GB) for various fine-tuning methods applied to the Llama-3-8B model across ten NLP tasks, as compared in the paper “Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets.” The vertical y-axis represents GPU Memory in GB, ranging from 0 to over 60, with major gridlines at 0, 20, 40, and 60. The horizontal x-axis lists six methods: “Full FT,” “MTL-FT,” “TAG,” “LoRA,” “QLoRA,” and “Ours,” each represented by a vertical bar. The first five bars are orange, while the final bar, labeled “Ours,” is green, visually distinguishing the proposed method. “Full FT” consumes the most memory, at approximately 70 GB. “MTL-FT” follows at about 40 GB, “TAG” and “LoRA” each use around 23–25 GB, and “QLoRA” uses roughly 15 GB. The “Ours” method uses approximately 24 GB, slightly more than QLoRA but significantly less than Full FT or MTL-FT. The chart visually supports the caption’s claim that the proposed method incurs only 9 GB more memory than QLoRA (which uses ~15 GB), aligning with the stated 24 GB usage, while achieving improved accuracy with substantially lower computation than Full FT.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm mit dem Titel „QLoRA“ vergleicht den GPU-Speicherbedarf in Gigabyte (GB) verschiedener Fine-Tuning-Methoden für das Sprachmodell Llama-3-8B auf zehn NLP-Aufgaben, wobei die horizontalen Achsen die Methoden „Full FT“, „MTL-FT“, „TAG“, „LoRA“, „QLoRA“ und „Ours“ in dieser Reihenfolge auflisten, während die vertikale Achse den GPU-Speicherbedarf in GB anzeigt, skaliert von 0 bis über 60 GB mit Tick-Markierungen in 20-GB-Schritten. Die Balken sind überwiegend orange, mit Ausnahme des letzten Balkens „Ours“, der grün ist und visuell hervorgehoben wird. Der „Full FT“-Balken ist am höchsten und erreicht etwa 70 GB, gefolgt vom „MTL-FT“-Balken bei etwa 40 GB, während „TAG“ und „LoRA“ jeweils bei etwa 22 GB liegen. Der „QLoRA“-Balken ist mit etwa 13 GB der niedrigste unter den orangefarbenen Balken, und der grüne „Ours“-Balken liegt bei etwa 22 GB, was eine moderate Erhöhung gegenüber QLoRA darstellt, jedoch deutlich unter den anderen Baselines bleibt. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern folgen der Reihenfolge der Methoden im Diagramm, wobei „Ours“ als letzter Balken positioniert ist und durch seine Farbe und den Kontext der Bildunterschrift als vorgeschlagener Ansatz hervorgehoben wird.
